items.title: Dance video: laughing with vs laughing at
items.pattern: laughing with someone vs laughing at them
items.relationship: Three friends in the same group
items.contrast: A shared laugh about A's dance video versus the group humiliating A over it.
items.cost_of_misread: If C asks for the link when A is upset, C joins the humiliation. If C tries to intervene during friendly teasing, C makes the room awkward.

version_1.label: Friends enjoying the video together
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A is proudly laughing along with the group's affection.
version_1.correct_next_move: Join the shared amusement and ask to see the video.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [embarrassed] [chuckles] I showed them my dance video.

version_2.label: A is being laughed at
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh covers embarrassment about people passing the video around.
version_2.correct_next_move: Stop the pile-on and offer practical support.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [worried] [sighs] I showed them my dance video.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] That sounds awful. Want me to ask them to stop passing it around?

items.title: Team lead: sarcasm vs sincere good news
items.pattern: irony or sarcasm vs sincere meaning
items.contrast: "Dream come true" as sincere excitement versus sarcastic resentment.
items.cost_of_misread: Congratulating A for an unwanted promotion feels tone-deaf. Treating genuine excitement as a complaint kills the celebration.

version_1.label: A genuinely wants the promotion
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A laughs with excited disbelief at good news.

version_2.label: A is being sarcastic
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's chuckle signals that the promotion means unwanted work.
version_2.correct_next_move: Recognize the burden and ask about the terms.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] That sounds like a pile of work. Did they raise your pay?

items.title: Bold presentation: scare quotes vs literal praise
items.contrast: The word "bold" as a polite dodge for criticism versus a genuine compliment.
items.cost_of_misread: Calling it a compliment when A was insulted dismisses the sting. Assuming criticism when A is proud undercuts A's achievement.

version_1.label: Bold is sincere praise
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's delighted laugh accepts the compliment.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [happy] That is a compliment. You took a real risk.

version_2.label: Bold is a scare-quoted insult
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's sarcastic chuckle marks "bold" as a softened way of saying bad.
version_2.correct_next_move: Name the likely slight rather than celebrating it.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Ouch. They were avoiding the word "bad."

items.title: Midnight pickup: real request vs a gag
items.pattern: a real request vs treated as a gag
items.setting: Friends making plans after a late shift
items.contrast: A playful imaginary pickup versus a genuine need for a ride.
items.cost_of_misread: Sending a joke response to a real midnight ride request leaves A stranded. Taking a clear bit literally makes a playful moment unnecessarily serious.

version_1.label: A is making a playful bit
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A laughs because the dramatic midnight pickup is part of the joke.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [playful] Can someone pick me up after my shift?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [playful] I will bring the royal carriage.

version_2.label: A needs an actual ride
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh softens a request A feels bad about making.
version_2.correct_next_move: Commit to helping and get the details.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] [worried] Can someone pick me up after my shift?

items.title: Corner office: celebration vs unwanted offer
items.pattern: genuine celebration vs hollow or unwanted news
items.contrast: A coveted office offer versus an offer that is being dressed up as a reward.
items.cost_of_misread: Throwing a celebration for an unwanted move makes A feel trapped. Treating a real win as a bad deal spoils it.

version_1.label: A loves the offer
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A laughs with excitement about the window and the new office.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [delighted] They offered me the corner office.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [excited] The one by the server room?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [happy] You got it! We are celebrating tonight.

version_2.label: A does not want the offer
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh points out the window as the thin silver lining.
version_2.correct_next_move: Recognize that the offer may be a bad trade and support refusal.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [disappointed] [sighs] They offered me the corner office.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [worried] The one by the server room?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] That sounds like a bad trade. You can say no.

items.title: Dinner touch: flirtation vs crossed boundary
items.pattern: playful flirt vs a boundary was crossed
items.contrast: An invited romantic touch versus an unwanted touch that lasted too long.
items.cost_of_misread: Keeping the flirtation going after an unwanted touch dismisses a boundary violation. Treating mutual flirtation as danger can embarrass A.

version_1.label: A enjoyed the flirtation
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A laughs with pleased excitement about Sam's interest.
version_1.correct_next_move: Ask about the romantic next step.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [delighted] [chuckles] Sam put a hand on my knee at dinner.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [playful] So, are you seeing Sam again?

version_2.label: A felt uncomfortable
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh is an attempt to make an invasive moment sound smaller.
version_2.correct_next_move: Validate the boundary and offer support.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [scared] Sam put a hand on my knee at dinner.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] That is not okay. Want me there next time?

items.title: Treatment schedule: dark coping vs no jokes
items.pattern: dark coping humor vs please stop I am not okay
items.contrast: A uses dark humor to cope versus A explicitly cannot tolerate jokes right now.
items.cost_of_misread: Joining the joke when A is overwhelmed is cruel. Refusing to play along when dark humor is helping can make A feel alone.

version_1.label: Dark humor helps A cope
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's sarcastic laugh invites the group to make the situation briefly manageable through humor.
version_1.correct_next_move: Match the dark humor while offering company.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [tired] The doctor says I need another round of treatment.

version_2.label: A cannot handle jokes
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's laugh breaks through tears and is followed by a direct limit.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [scared] [sighs] The doctor says I need another round of treatment.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [crying] [nervous laugh] Great. My calendar loves me. Please, no jokes.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [softly] Okay. No jokes. I am here.

items.title: After the meeting: affiliation vs raw feelings
items.pattern: warm affiliation vs brushing off something still raw
items.contrast: A's laugh accepts care from the group versus A uses laughter to brush away feelings that are still raw.
items.cost_of_misread: Pushing for a deep talk during warm closure can overdo the moment. Treating raw distress as resolved leaves A unsupported.

version_1.label: A feels held by the group
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A laughs warmly at a self-description because the group stayed close.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [warmly] Thanks for staying after the meeting.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [warmly] You were not alone. We stayed because we care.

version_2.label: A is still hurting
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's nervous laugh tries to close down feelings that have not settled.
version_2.correct_next_move: Give A permission to keep talking.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sad] [sighs] Thanks for staying after the meeting.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] You do not have to laugh it off. Want to talk?

items.title: Garlic bread: affectionate teasing vs hurtful teasing
items.pattern: affectionate teasing vs the target is actually hurt
items.contrast: A familiar food joke that B enjoys versus the same line landing as a cutting criticism.
items.cost_of_misread: Joining the roast when B is hurt makes B feel ganged up on. Correcting a friendly ritual joke makes the interaction oddly heavy.

version_1.label: B enjoys the teasing
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: B's big laugh claims the cooking mistake as a running joke.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [playful] You burned the garlic bread again.

version_2.label: B feels criticized
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: B's nervous laugh covers embarrassment after A's annoyed remark.
version_2.correct_next_move: Interrupt the criticism and reassure B.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [annoyed] You burned the garlic bread again.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Hey, that came out harsh. B, dinner was good.

items.title: Jordan and the budget: in-joke vs accusation
items.pattern: in-joke or conspiracy vs a serious accusation
items.contrast: A fake office conspiracy versus a genuine suspicion that B leaked budget information.
items.cost_of_misread: Treating a possible leak as a joke fails to contain a serious accusation. Treating a group in-joke as misconduct creates needless tension.

version_1.label: A fake conspiracy bit
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's big laugh reveals that the supposed secret is a shared office joke.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [playful] I saw you leave the meeting with Jordan.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [amused] You told Jordan about the budget?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [laughs] Finally. Can I join the fake conspiracy?

version_2.label: A suspects a real leak
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's sarcastic chuckle signals anger, not amusement, about confidential information.
version_2.correct_next_move: Slow down the accusation and establish facts.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [angry] I saw you leave the meeting with Jordan.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [worried] You told Jordan about the budget?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [worried] Let us check what Jordan heard before anyone gets blamed.
